transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-05 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya(PDX AE), Jonah(SE), Elena(CSM) — Sarah(BlueArc Eng Lead), Tom(Platform), Priya(SRE), Amit(PO)

Summary (auto): Quick recap of yesterday's 18:37 spike — saw increased tail p99 to ~1.2s and a small cluster of 503/504s correlated with queue depth. Focus: tuning retry budget, avoid retry storms, warm up KV cache, and validate VPC egress list.

[00:00] Maya: hi everyone, thanks for joining, morning, afternoon depending where you are, we're here for the weekly pilot check-in. quick agenda — rca of last nights spike, retry budget proposal, kv cache warmup and vpc egress check.
[00:18] Sarah: hey Maya, thanks. yeah we saw that spike right after our batch jobs kicked off, we started seeing elevated p99 and roughly 40 5xx during a 6-minute window, so want to understand cause and fix.
[00:30] Jonah: right — we pulled traces, and there's a pattern where the queue depth on a handful of shards hit a sudden high which pushed some requests into slower execution paths; also noticed more prefix-miss on the kv cache for that period.
[00:44] Tom: just to add, our overnight batch hits an internal feature flag endpoint that fans out many small prompts, maybe that generated a hotkey. we tried to move the window but it's business-critical so we need a mitigation without shifting the window.
[00:58] Priya: and we also saw a bump in TCP retransmits on the node agents which could be unrelated but thought to mention it.
[01:10] Jonah: yep, so three hypotheses: 1) client-side hotkey causing microburst, 2) KV cache coldness causing higher decode time, 3) transient network egress/policy causing retries and queueing. possibly a combination.
[01:30] Maya: for the microburst, our recommended approach is adaptive retry budgeting on the client side — keep a small initial retry budget and backoff aggressively on 5xx/timeout. we shared a sample config last week but I'll send a more detailed worksheet after the call.
[01:47] Sarah: when you say retry budget, is that server-side or client-side? we currently have client code that retries up to 3 times with exponential backoff.
[01:57] Jonah: it's client-side primarily; you control the retry windows. the idea is to set a shared budget per user-agent/tenant and avoid bursty parallel retries. in practice, that means request-level jitter, max parallelism, and a decaying token bucket.
[02:18] Sarah: okay... our current library doesn't support decaying token buckets; would need work. Amit: (interruption) how urgent is this — do we need code changes before the next spike?
[02:30] Maya: short answer, no immediate code commit required — we can implement guardrails at the infra level: Redwood can apply rate-windowing and soft-failover to a cheaper model variant during spikes so you get graceful degradation while engineering ship the client library changes.
[02:45] Tom: that soft-failover — does it preserve response shape? e.g., do we still get the same JSON schema so our downstream doesn't break?
[02:53] Jonah: yep, we can preserve schema and optionally tag responses with metadata like "fallback_model":"vicuna-7b-ql" (note: voice recognition sometimes transcribed model names incorrectly). there may be differences in quality but shape stays the same.
[03:10] Priya: we need clear SLO for that fallback — we can't silently degrade beyond a certain quality threshold for regulatory reasons. also audit logs for every fallback event.
[03:21] Elena: Redwood Console already provides per-request tags and a fallback event log; we can push an alert to your SRE Slack channel when a fallback occurs.
[03:30] Sarah: good. back to kv cache — Jon, you said prefix-miss spiked; is that a cold-start for the cache?
[03:37] Jonah: yeah, we saw many cache-miss patterns aligned with the first few requests to some model shards. probable cause: shard rebalancing + cold cache. the runtime has a KV cache that stores prefix context; when it's cold decode time increases ~30-60ms per token for affected shards.
[03:55] Sarah: 30-60ms per token sounds small but it multiplied across long sequences and p99 it adds up. can you pre-warm?
[04:03] Jonah: we have a warmup probe feature — you can configure a set of prefix prompts to pre-populate caches on spin-up or after redeploys. we can also enable a short-lived prefetch window during expected batch times. we'll export our recommended warmup set for the patterns you showed.
[04:20] Tom: will warmup impact costs significantly? we have to justify charges to finance.
[04:26] Maya: minimal — prefetch probes are very small requests, and we can do them with a cached/cheap variant so cost is usually negligible compared to preventing 5xx/large retries.
[04:36] Priya: there's another angle: our egress/NAT gateway has aggressive connection tracking rules and sometimes drops long-lived flows, which could surface as timeouts. we can share iptables rules.
[04:49] Tom: yes, that's why we wanted to validate CIDRs for Redwood's peering to avoid breaks.
[04:56] Maya: action: Tom share the egress rules and we'll run a validation.
[05:01] Amit: do you see any evidence that backend throttles were triggered on Redwood side?
[05:07] Jonah: we saw no global throttle events in the platform metrics. the throttles we saw were at the per-shard queue level because of local queueing — so it's more micro-shard saturation than tenant-level throttle.
[05:20] Sarah: ok that suggests adaptive routing could help? route some requests to less loaded region?
[05:26] Jonah: yes we can route by policy; Redwood supports routing by latency and by capacity. for pilot we can enable cross-shard fallback to a cold-standby pool for high-latency requests.
[05:40] Sarah: what's the expected failover latency — immediate?
[05:44] Jonah: it's near-immediate for compatible model variants; for model variants with different tokenizer or size there might be an extra 20-100ms.
[05:52] Maya: quick pause — any questions on SOC2/PL certs? Priya earlier asked about audit logs during fallback events.
[06:01] Priya: yes we need audit logs sent to our SIEM and they need to include request_id, tenant_id, fallback_reason.
[06:08] Elena: we can stream Redwood audit logs to S3 or push to your SIEM via HTTPS sink; we'll include request_id, model_variant, fallback_reason and timestamps.
[06:18] Tom: do you also support KMS/HSM key rotation? our compliance team insists on HSM backed keys.
[06:24] Maya: yes — Private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM; for dedicated we offer KMS integration. we'll include the options in the security pack we send.
[06:34] Sarah: great. back to retry budget details — can you run through a sample config?
[06:39] Jonah: sure — here's an example (verbatim): initial_attempt, then up to 2 retries with base backoff 100ms + jitter, max backoff 1500ms, per-tenant token bucket of 5 tokens decaying 1 token per 10s; on 5xx, deduct 2 tokens. if tokens exhausted, fail-fast or route to fallback.
[07:05] Sarah: that seems reasonable; question: if our client is in Javascript browser, will this work? our front end sometimes retries for UX reasons.
[07:14] Maya: for browser clients, we recommend limiting retries in the browser and moving retry logic to server side to avoid coordinated bursts.
[07:21] Amit: we can't move everything server-side right away — some clients need quick fixes. is there a temporary server-side guard you can put?
[07:28] Jonah: yes, we can enforce per-API-key concurrency limits at the gateway and early reject or queue requests, which reduces blast radius.
[07:36] Priya: okay, so combining client token bucket + server concurrency limit + warmup + adaptive routing — seems like a multi-layer plan.
[07:45] Maya: exactly, defense in depth.
[07:48] Sarah: on telemetry — can we get an export of traces for the 18:37 spike? we want spans and raw request bodies redacted.
[07:56] Jonah: yes, we'll export traces with PII redacted; we'll include full timing for p50/p95/p99 and per-shard queue lengths.
[08:06] Maya: Jonah will drop the dashboards and a short doc in the shared drive.
[08:10] Jonah: noted.
[08:12] Sarah: what about client-side idempotency keys — do they help?
[08:16] Jonah: yes for reruns; idempotency avoids duplicate side-effects but doesn't prevent retry storms unless combined with a token bucket.
[08:24] Tom: small tangent — competitor product X does circuit-breaker at the edge; do you support circuit-breakers?
[08:31] Jonah: we do — config options include circuit-breaker thresholds by latency and by error-rate. we prefer adaptive circuit-breaker combined with retry budget.
[08:41] Priya: one more operational ask: can Redwood provide a playbook snippet we can hook to our incident runbook? e.g., triage steps, dashboards to check, recommended patching.
[08:50] Elena: yes, we have a pilot runbook template we'll share — includes quick commands and checks for kv cache, queue depth, and fallback events.
[08:58] Sarah: brilliant.
[09:00] Amit: timeline — we need this sorted before end of next week; can we commit to configuration changes and the controlled test?
[09:08] Maya: yes: by 2026-08-07 we'll share retry sheet and configs; by 2026-08-09 you'll run the controlled spike and upload traces; Redwood will run a mirrored soft-failover test during that window.
[09:20] Tom: one last q: cost implications of using a fallback model — do you have an estimate?
[09:26] Jonah: fallback to smaller variants reduces token cost by ~40-60% for long sequences; we'll include a cost delta example in the spreadsheet.
[09:34] Sarah: ok thanks, that's helpful.
[09:36] Maya: any blockers?
[09:38] Priya: none immediate — just need docs and the egress CIDRs.
[09:42] Maya: perfect. quick recap of action items and owners.
[09:46] Elena: I'll create the ticket in your shared workspace with links to docs.
[09:50] Tom: and I'll get the firewall rules over.
[09:53] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up mid-week.
[09:56] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: some model names and acronyms may be mis-transcribed (e.g., vicuna vs vectra), speaker labels may be generic in parts.

References shared during call: retry-budget-spreadsheet.xlsx (link: drive/BAH/retry-budget.xlsx), kv-cache-dashboard (link: console/BAH/pilot/kv-cache), security-pack.pdf (link: drive/BAH/security-pack.pdf).
